headline: Japan Nominal Wages Rise at Fastest Pace in Nearly 30 Years
summary: Japan's nominal wages rose 4.6 percent in September compared to the previous year, marking the largest gain since 1997.
why: Wage growth is a critical metric for the Bank of Japan in evaluating inflation trends and considering potential shifts in monetary policy.

impacts.name: Japan
impacts.why: Nominal wage growth accelerated to its highest rate since 1997.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Japanese wage figures moved markets by signaling potential changes in domestic consumption and monetary policy outlook.
